{{Short description|American physicist}}
'''Rodney Lee Cool''' (March 8, 1920 &ndash; April 16, 1988) was an American physicist who helped to establish the existence of the [[quark]].
<ref name="NAP">[http://www.nap.edu/readingroom.php?book=biomems&page=rcool.html National Academies Press, Biographical Memoirs, Rodney Lee Cool, By Robert K. Adair]</ref>
<ref name="NYT">[https://www.nytimes.com/1988/04/20/obituaries/rodney-l-cool-68-experimental-physicist.html?scp=1&sq=%22Rodney%20L.%20Cool%22&st=cse New York Times:Rodney L. Cool, 68, Experimental Physicist, April 20, 1988]</ref>
Cool was a professor of high-energy physics at Rockefeller University,<ref name="NYT"/> a member of the [[National Academies of Sciences]].<ref name="NAP"/><ref>[https://www.nytimes.com/1979/11/11/archives/marriage-announcement-23-no-title.html?sq=%2522Rodney%2520Lee%2520Cool%2522&scp=1&st=cse New York Times:Marriage Announcement 23 -- No Title, November 11, 1979]</ref>
He was also a Fellow of the [[American Physical Society]].<ref name="NYT"/>
Cool founded an experimental physics group at [[Rockefeller University]] in 1970.<ref name="NYT"/>

== Life and career ==
Cool graduated with a bachelor's degree from the [[University of South Dakota]] and received his M.S. and Ph.D. degrees from [[Harvard University]].<ref name="NYT"/>
He also worked at European Organization for Nuclear Research in Geneva. There he and his colleagues performed experiments that showed the quark to be a building block of [[neutrons]] and [[protons]].<ref name="NAP"/><ref name="NYT"/>
